title: IB English Mock Exam Prep: November Study Plan
summary: Prepare for November IB English mocks with a focused four-week plan for Paper 1, Paper 2, timed practice, feedback, quotes, and exam strategy.
body_markdown:
Preparing for a November English mock should focus on three priorities: confirming which papers your school will test, practising analytical writing under time pressure, and correcting recurring weaknesses. Effective **IB English mock exam prep** is active, so spend more time planning, writing, comparing, and reviewing than rereading notes.


This guide covers **IB English A: Literature** and **IB English A: Language and Literature** at SL and HL. Mocks are school-set assessments, not official IB examination sessions, so always confirm the scope, texts, timings, and permitted materials with your teacher.


### Confirm what your November mock will assess


The courses have similar examination structures, although their Paper 1 material differs. The official[Language A: Literature subject brief](https://www.ibo.org/contentassets/5895a05412144fe890312bad52b17044/curriculum.brief-languagea.literature-eng.pdf) and[Language A: Language and Literature subject brief](https://www.ibo.org/contentassets/5895a05412144fe890312bad52b17044/curriculum.brief-languagea.language.and.literature-eng.pdf) summarize the formal assessment structure.


Component Standard level Higher level Main task


Paper 1 1 hour 15 minutes, one of two passages 2 hours 15 minutes, both passages Guided analysis of unseen material


Paper 2 1 hour 45 minutes 1 hour 45 minutes Comparative essay on two studied literary works


Literature Paper 1 uses unseen **literary passages** , while Language and Literature uses unseen **non-literary passages** from different text types. Paper 2 offers four general questions, with students answering one using two studied literary works.


Your school may shorten a paper, assess only one component, or restrict Paper 2 to particular works. These arrangements do not alter the official format, but they should determine your immediate revision priorities.


### A four-week IB English mock exam prep plan


### Four weeks before: diagnose and organize


Complete one Paper 1 response and one Paper 2 plan without extensive preparation. Use the results to identify weaknesses in interpretation, analysis, organization, evidence, language, or timing.


Create an error log with three columns: **problem** , **evidence from my writing** , and **specific correction** . Replace vague comments such as “analysis is descriptive” with an action, for example: “After each quotation, explain how a specific word or structural choice shapes meaning.” The[IB English A Language and Literature resource hub](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-english-langlit-new) can help you review assessment components.


For Paper 2, select two or three effective work pairings. Build comparison grids covering themes, relationships, narrative or dramatic methods, structure, setting, context, and important contrasts.


### Three weeks before: practise individual skills


Divide each paper into short drills. For Paper 1, try these tasks:


- Annotate an unseen text and identify its central tension in **10 minutes** .
- Write a thesis and three-point plan in **10 minutes** .
- Produce one analytical paragraph in **20 minutes** , then revise it.


A strong paragraph connects **authorial choice, precise evidence, effect, and wider meaning** . Do not merely state that repetition creates emphasis. Explain what is repeated, how the pattern influences the audience, and why that effect supports the text’s purpose.


For Paper 2, create 4-6 comparison categories for each pairing. Apply them to unfamiliar prompts from the[Paper 2 Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-english-langlit-new/ib-english-langlit-english-paper-2/questionbank) . Your knowledge must remain flexible enough to answer the assigned question rather than reproduce a memorized essay.


### Two weeks before: practise under time pressure


Complete at least one full timed paper without a phone, unauthorized notes, or pauses. Use the official[IB sample examination papers](https://ibo.org/programmes/diploma-programme/assessment-and-exams/sample-exam-papers/) to examine authentic task wording. The[IB English Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-english-langlit-new/questionbank) provides additional targeted practice.


Review each attempt promptly. Identify one strength and no more than three weaknesses, then rewrite the weakest thesis or paragraph. Careful correction is usually more valuable than immediately producing another complete essay.


### Final week: rehearse, then reduce the load


Complete your final simulation about **4-6 days** before the mock. During the remaining days, rotate shorter tasks:


- Recall Paper 2 quotations and textual moments.
- Plan responses to unfamiliar questions.
- Annotate a short unseen text.
- Rewrite weak thesis statements.
- Review your error log.


The day before the mock, avoid another full paper. Check quotations, comparison categories, timing decisions, and equipment, then protect your sleep.


### How to revise for Paper 1


Paper 1 rewards interpretation supported by close analysis, not the number of techniques identified. Establish the text type, audience, purpose, tone, and central idea. Then investigate patterns such as tonal shifts, recurring imagery, contrasts, perspective, visual hierarchy, or structural turning points.


Organize paragraphs around ideas rather than isolated devices. Use the guiding question to control your argument, ensuring that each paragraph supports a focused thesis. The[RevisionDojo English study notes](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-english-langlit-new/notes) can help you review textual features and essay structure before practising independently.


### How to revise for Paper 2


Paper 2 requires sustained comparison, not two disconnected essays. Structure each paragraph around a shared issue, then examine how and why the authors treat it similarly or differently.


Memorize short, adaptable quotations alongside precise scenes, structural developments, characterization, narrative perspective, and motifs. When planning, test every idea against the exact wording of the question. A prompt about conflict, for example, requires analysis of how conflict is constructed and why it matters, not merely a list of conflicts.


### Common November mock mistakes


Avoid these habits:


- **Rereading instead of producing:** Recognition does not train essay construction.
- **Technique spotting:** Naming devices without explaining meaning produces shallow analysis.
- **Ignoring the question:** A polished prepared essay remains ineffective if it misses the prompt.
- **Separating Paper 2 works:** Discussing one work and then the other weakens comparison.
- **Overusing quotations:** Brief evidence with detailed analysis is usually more effective.
- **Skipping review:** Unreviewed practice allows recurring weaknesses to continue.


Convert feedback into the next practice task. If organization is weak, produce plans and topic sentences. If analysis lacks depth, rewrite a paragraph with closer attention to individual words and structural effects.


### Exam-day strategy


Read every instruction and choose carefully when options are provided. Reserve planning time because a clear argument prevents repetition later. Keep checking that each paragraph answers the question, and prioritize a complete analytical argument over an unnecessarily long introduction. Leave several minutes to correct unclear wording, missing comparisons, and sentence errors.


### Conclusion


Strong **IB English mock exam prep** combines accurate assessment knowledge, repeated planning, timed writing, and focused correction. Confirm your school’s November format, progress from short drills to realistic simulations, and reduce the workload before the exam.
